items.stem: Look at the food chain: grass, grasshopper, frog, snake. Which organism is the producer?

explain.why: A grasshopper cannot make its own food. It eats grass, so it is a consumer.
A frog eats other animals, so it is a consumer.
A snake eats other animals, so it is a consumer.

solution: A producer makes its own food. Only the green plant, grass, does that.

items.stem: What does the arrow in a food chain show?
options: Energy passing from the animal to the food it eats
The direction in which the animal walks
The bigger animal pointing at the smaller one
Energy passing from the food to the animal that eats it

explain.why: The arrow points to the eater, not to the food.
The arrows show feeding, not movement.
The size of the animals does not decide the direction.

solution: The arrow points from the food to the organism that eats it, in the direction energy flows.

items.stem: Which of the following is a producer?

explain.why: A cow eats grass, so it is a consumer.
A bird eats seeds or insects, so it is a consumer.
A fish eats other living things, so it is a consumer.

solution: A mango tree is a green plant that makes its own food using light.

items.stem: In the food chain grass, grasshopper, frog, which organism is the prey of the frog?

explain.why: The frog does not eat grass.
A frog is the predator here, not its own prey.
The Sun is not an animal that the frog eats.

solution: The frog eats the grasshopper, so the grasshopper is its prey.

items.stem: In the food chain algae, water flea, small fish, big fish, which organism is the predator of the small fish?

explain.why: Algae are producers. They do not eat fish.
The water flea is eaten by the small fish.
The small fish is the prey, not its own predator.

solution: The big fish eats the small fish, so it is the predator.

items.stem: Where does the energy at the start of most food chains come from?

explain.why: Soil gives plants minerals, but not the energy they need to make food.
Plants need water, but it is not their source of energy.
Plants use gases from the air, but the energy comes from the Sun.

solution: Plants take in light energy from the Sun to make food, and animals get this energy when they eat.

items.stem: Which of the following is a non-living thing that affects how fish survive in a pond?
options: The other fish in the pond

explain.why: Plants are living things.
Other fish are living things.
Insects are living things.

solution: Temperature is not a living thing, but it affects how fish survive.

items.stem: Which of the following is a living factor that can affect the survival of a rabbit?

explain.why: Rain is not a living thing.
Temperature is not a living thing.
Sunlight is not a living thing.

solution: Predators such as foxes are living things that affect the rabbits.

items.stem: A pond dries up in a very long dry spell. What will most likely happen to the fish that live in it?
options: They die because they cannot live out of water
They fly away to another pond nearby
They grow legs and walk to another pond
They live on the dry land around the pond

explain.why: Fish do not have wings and cannot leave the water.
Fish cannot change their bodies in a short time.
Fish need water to breathe, so they cannot live on dry land.

solution: Fish cannot move out of a pond that has dried up and cannot breathe on land, so they die.

items.stem: Which of the following moves to another place when the weather becomes unfavourable?
options: A tree that sheds all its leaves in the dry season
A snail that stays inside its shell until it rains
A mushroom that grows again on a rotting log
A bird that flies to a warmer country in winter

explain.why: A tree cannot move. It stays where it is.
The snail stays in the same place.
A mushroom cannot move.

solution: Birds can fly, so they move to places where the weather and food are better.

items.stem: Which of the following food chains is correct?

explain.why: A rabbit does not feed the grass. Grass must come first.
The chain is written the wrong way round.
An eagle does not feed a rabbit.

solution: Grass is eaten by the rabbit, and the rabbit is eaten by the eagle.

items.stem: In the food chain lettuce, caterpillar, bird, which organism does the bird eat?

explain.why: The bird in this chain does not eat lettuce.
The bird does not eat itself.
The arrow shows the bird eats the caterpillar.

solution: The arrow from the caterpillar points to the bird, so the bird eats the caterpillar.

items.stem: Look at the food web. Which organisms does the snake eat?

explain.why: These are eaten by the rabbit and the frog, not by the snake.
The hawk eats the snake, not the other way round.
There is also an arrow from the rabbit to the snake.

solution: Arrows from the frog and the rabbit point to the snake.

items.stem: A pot plant is not watered for two weeks. What will most likely happen to it?
options: It makes more food than before
It grows roots on its leaves

explain.why: A plant needs water to grow.
Without water it cannot make food well.
Plants do not grow new roots in response to dry soil in a short time.

solution: Plants need water to stay alive and to make food.

items.stem: Which of the following is a decomposer?

explain.why: A grasshopper eats living plants.
A rose bush makes its own food.
A hawk hunts living animals.

solution: A mushroom is a fungus that feeds on dead plants and animals.

items.stem: What do decomposers do in an environment?
options: They feed on dead living things and return nutrients to the soil
They make their own food from water using light energy
They hunt living animals and eat them for food
They eat only living plants and their fruits

explain.why: That is what producers do.
That is what predators do.
That is what some animals do. Decomposers feed on dead things.

solution: Decomposers break down dead remains, and the nutrients go back into the soil for plants.

items.stem: Why are green plants called producers?
options: They eat the food that animals leave
They produce more animals than any other living thing
They take in food from the soil
They make their own food using light energy

explain.why: Plants do not eat food.
Plants do not produce animals.
Plants take water and minerals from the soil, not food.

solution: Plants use light energy to make food from water and a gas from the air.

items.stem: Mei counts more snails in a garden bed that has a lot of lettuce than in a bed with none. Which factor most likely explains this?
options: The time of day she counted

explain.why: Colour does not decide how many snails can live there.
The beds are about the same size and size does not explain the difference.
Time of day would not explain the difference between beds.

solution: Snails eat lettuce, so more snails can live where there is more food.

items.stem: Which animal competes with a rabbit for grass?

explain.why: An eagle is a predator of the rabbit. It does not eat grass.
A snake is a predator of the rabbit. It does not eat grass.
A frog eats insects and does not eat grass.

solution: The goat and the rabbit both need the same food.

items.stem: A frog is kept in a dry box with no water for many days. Which factor is affecting the frog?

explain.why: Nothing in the story says the light changed.
The story is about the lack of water.
The colour of a box does not affect a frog's survival.

solution: Frogs need a damp place, and a lack of water makes it hard for them to survive.

items.stem: Look at the food web. If all the grasshoppers die, what will happen to the number of frogs at first?
options: It will decrease because the frogs have less food
It will increase because there is less competition
It will stay the same because frogs eat plants
It will increase because the snakes eat fewer frogs

explain.why: The frogs do not compete with the grasshoppers. They eat them.
In this web the frogs eat only grasshoppers.
The snakes still eat frogs, and the frogs now have no food.

solution: The frogs eat only grasshoppers in this web, so they would have no food and their number would fall.

items.stem: Some animals sleep through the cold winter when food is hard to find. How does this help them to survive?
options: They find more food while they are asleep in the cold
They grow much bigger while they sleep
They stay warm by lying in the sun all day
They use less energy while there is little food

explain.why: They do not look for food when they sleep.
Sleeping does not make them grow bigger.
They sleep in shelters and are not in the sun.

solution: Sleeping uses very little energy, so the animal can live on the food stored in its body.

items.stem: Many trees drop their leaves in the dry season. How does this help them to survive?
options: The tree can make more food
The tree takes in more light

explain.why: Without leaves the tree makes less food.
Without leaves the tree takes in less light.
Losing leaves does not make a tree taller.

solution: Water leaves a tree through its leaves, so having no leaves saves water.

items.stem:
Which of the following statements about a food chain are correct?
A: A producer makes its own food.
B: A consumer cannot make its own food.
C: Energy flows from the consumer to the producer.
D: A food chain can start with a predator.

explain.why: Energy flows from the producer to the consumers, so C is wrong.
A food chain starts with a producer, so D is wrong.
Both are wrong.

solution: A and B are correct. Energy flows from the producer to the consumers.

items.stem: Which statement about energy in a food chain is correct?
options: Energy from the Sun is trapped by the producer and passed on to the consumers
Energy from the Sun is trapped by the consumers and passed on to the producer
Energy is made by the animals at the top of the chain
Energy goes back to the Sun at the end of the chain

explain.why: Only plants can use light energy to make food.
Animals do not make energy. They get it from their food.
Energy does not return to the Sun.

solution: Plants trap light from the Sun, and animals get energy by eating plants or other animals.

explain.why: S eats Q and R. P is eaten by Q and R, and T eats S.
S does not eat P, and R is also eaten by S.
T is the predator of S. It is not its prey.

solution: Arrows from Q and R point to S.

items.stem: Why does every food chain begin with a producer?
options: Producers are always the biggest living things
Only producers can make food using light energy
Producers eat the animals that die
Producers are the only things that need energy

explain.why: Many producers are small, such as algae.
Producers do not eat animals.
All living things need energy.

solution: Consumers get their energy from food. The first food has to be made by a producer from light energy.

items.stem:
Which of the following statements are correct about living things when their environment becomes unfavourable?
A: Some animals move to other places.
B: Some plants die.
C: All living things change their bodies in a day.
D: Living things do not need to react.

explain.why: Bodies cannot change in a day, so C is wrong.
Living things are affected, so D is wrong.
Both are wrong.

solution: Animals can move away and some plants die. Bodies do not change in a day.

items.stem: Some rabbits are brought to an island with plenty of grass and no animals that eat rabbits. What will most likely happen to the grass over time?
options: The grass will increase as the rabbits increase
The grass will increase because the rabbits drop seeds
The grass will decrease as the rabbits increase

explain.why: More rabbits eat more grass.
The rabbits eat grass, so its amount changes.
Rabbits eat much more grass than seeds they could drop.

solution: With no predators, the rabbits increase and eat more grass.

items.stem: A lot of fertiliser washes into a pond and the algae grow very fast, then die. Soon the fish in the pond die. Which is the most likely reason?
options: The algae eat the fish when they die
The decomposers make the water hotter than the fish can stand
Decomposers feed on the dead algae and use up the oxygen in the water
The fish eat so many algae that they run out of food

explain.why: Algae are producers. They do not eat fish.
The main problem is the loss of oxygen.
There were a lot of algae, so the fish did not run short of food.

solution: Many dead algae feed the decomposers, which use up the oxygen that the fish need.

items.stem: What would happen to a forest if there were no decomposers?
options: The plants would grow faster because there would be more space
Dead things would pile up and nutrients would not return to the soil
The animals would stop eating and soon all die
The producers would make less food because of too much light

explain.why: Plants need the nutrients that decomposers return to the soil.
Animals need food whether or not decomposers are present.
Light is not the problem. Nutrients would run low.

solution: Decomposers break down dead things and return nutrients to the soil.

items.stem: Look at the food web. If all the frogs die, which organisms are affected directly?

explain.why: Frogs are not connected to the plants directly.
The mouse and the owl do not eat frogs and are not eaten by them.
These do not feed on or feed the frog.

solution: Grasshoppers are no longer eaten by the frogs, and snakes lose a food source.
